body: @KeyC0de Thank you for the report, please attach .fbx 3D model file affected by the problem to this issue so others can reproduce and investigate

Unfortunately, the fbx in question is closed source and I can't share it on here.
But I will describe the situation as clearly as I can below.

The .fbx is for a skeletal mesh character.
The aiScene has 5 `aiMesh`es, head, body, eyes, eyelashes, hair.
The model contains 55 morph targets (mAnimMeshes).
Of these about 8 are for the eyes aiMesh, 8 for the body aiMesh and the rest are for the head aiMesh.
These Morphs are configured correctly in external programs like Unreal Engine, Blender & 3ds Max that I've checked - meaning the corresponding morph targets appear only for the meshes they belong in and they morph the original mesh properly.
The morphs are also imported and work fine in my engine, using assimp.

So what is the problem?
It's that there's not a proper 1-1 correspondence between an aiAnimMesh and the aiMesh which it morphs. In other words a morph target for eyes appears on every aiMesh in the .fbx scene, so the eyes aiMesh (correct), the body aiMesh (incorrect), the head aiMesh (incorrect), the hair aiMesh (incorrect) etc.
Same for all other morph targets.
Ergo when I end up loading all the aiMeshes properly, the end result is, that instead of having 55 mAnimMeshes, i have like 200+.

Now if I select the proper aiMesh that an mAnimMesh belongs to and change the weight of the morph that morph itself works as intended on the aiMesh. But that'll also be possible for another aiMesh in the scene and if I change the morph's weight on that other animMesh it'll morph some random vertices (that happen to be the same indices as the indices morphing the proper aiMesh's morph target).

It is somewhat frustrating and a waste of memory resources.

I have thoroughly debugged and investigated the problem and my code and I can confirm it's a bug with Assimp during the import process, assimp simply cannot distinguish properly which aiMesh an mAnimMesh belongs to.
And as I saw in the code, aiAnimMesh doesn't contain a pointer to the aiMesh it 'originates from'. I figure that something of that sort should probably happen to fix this issue.

[Another example: if I load up a simpler single aiMesh .fbx model file using assimp with a few morphs (i tried exporting a monkey from Blender & Unreal Engine and importing it into my Engine via Assimp) then all morphs appear on that single aiMesh and they all work fine.]

Although I can't share the .fbx I would be very much willing to debug the issue myself though if you could provide instructions or a mini-guide.

If you need something else, I can assist you further.

@KeyC0de Thank you for the detailed explanation.

It seems unlikely any devs would attempt work on this task unless there was a model which demonstrated the problem.  Since you currently are very familiar with the problem space and also able to use blender, I might suggest the following in order to maximize chances that someone would pick this up...

- Create a new model consisting of a couple of primitives e.g. a torus and a cylinder or sphere.
- Add 2 morph/blendshape meshes for the torus (keep it simple, scale up/down or something easy)
- Add 3 morph/blendshape meshes for the other (cylinder/sphere) primitive; again keep the shapes simple, just move a few random vertices around or shear the mesh etc to avoid spending more time than necessary
- Result will hopefully be a very lightweight model which demonstrates the problem when loaded via assimp, and which can be freely shared (having different numbers of blendshapes for each of the meshes will aid reasoning when troubleshooting)

Of course, if you already have an open source model with blendshapes, could start with that and add a second mesh with its own new blendshapes, doesn't need to be fancy as long as the problem is reproducible.

The other benefit of having a lightweight, open source model is that it can then be used for adding unit tests to prevent regressions in future.
I will try to find a free model with multiple meshes and morph targets to share here after I verify the issue with it in my engine.
Im down to pick this up, been doing some file format parsing and animation work recently. @KeyC0de when you have a model to reproduce the bug I'd be able to better understand what's going on.

I'm afraid I haven't had the chance to get back on this on a timely manner.
But fear not, I won't forget it.
Hopefully in the near future i'll be able to test this scenario with another similar model, OR in the case I can't reproduce it, I'll find what the problem is with my particular model and post a solution here regardless.
